cards.title: k74 · Know who did it — staff names and PINs
cards.note: Right now the whole app shares one passcode, so every action is anonymous. Inventory and orders are worthless if you cannot see who moved what or took which order. Small fix: staff pick their name and a short PIN when they start work, and that name is recorded on every stock line, order and payment. Cheap now, painful to add later.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k72 · Housekeeping room board — cleaning status and notes
cards.note: A board for room state: Clean · Being cleaned · Needs cleaning · Maintenance, with who and when. After a guest checks out, staff tick what they used, replaced or lost — those become stock lines, and a lost or damaged item can optionally be added to the guest's tab. The existing cleaning checklist slots in here; it just needs the room-state link.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
Connection to the date-block work (plan for the toolbar Block button is on its own card): a "Cleaning" block on the calendar should itself create the cleaning job for that room + date, so staff never enter the same job twice. Once the job is marked cleaned and checked, the calendar pill should turn green ("Cleaned") and offer to open the room again. Only Cleaning spawns a job — Maintenance and Owner-use blocks just block.

Shape to change: today one row = one item (pick from a fixed list, then retype room / date / cleaned by / checked by for every item). The real job is one cleaning per room per day, with the items ticked inside it — replaced (bed sheet, towel) vs restocked (toothbrush, toothpaste) vs lost.

Bug found while checking this: cleaning and inventory saves cannot reach the database. Both tables declare id uuid, but the app builds ids like 'clean-1755432…' and 'inv-1755432…' (HousekeepingTab.tsx lines 54 and 34). Postgres rejects those, the error is only console.error'd, and everything falls back to that one browser's localStorage — so staff entries are per-device and invisible to anyone else. Fix the id generation (a real UUID) before this board is relied on.

cards.title: k75 · Navigation: group the tabs into the four parts (Option B)
cards.note:
Make the top bar one tab per part, with the detail inside as sub-tabs, so the bar stays six tabs no matter how much gets built:
• Front desk — Calendar (opens here) · Bookings · Guests & Partners
• Restaurant — Orders · Menu
• Inventory — Stock · Recipes · Suppliers · Counts
• Housekeeping — Rooms · Cleaning checklist
• Money — Payments · Expenses · Purchases · Performance
• Settings — Rates · Staff · Accounts
Nothing is hidden: the sub-tabs are visible as soon as the tab opens, and Calendar stays the landing screen so front-desk staff click once. Every future feature goes inside its part instead of adding another top tab. Do this AFTER the restaurant and inventory exist, so nothing is reorganised while it is still being built. Later (once staff PINs land) tabs can follow the person: kitchen sees Restaurant + Inventory, manager sees everything.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k71 · Inventory system — food, drinks and hotel supplies
cards.note: One stock room shared by the kitchen and the hotel: food, drinks, linens, toiletries. Every item in and out is logged with who and when. Recipes are the important part — a dish is made of ingredients, so selling one dish takes its ingredients off the shelf automatically, no manual deducting. Plus low-stock alerts, suppliers, and a regular physical count so the numbers stay honest. Housekeeping's "used, replaced, lost" writes into this same log.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k73 · Money and performance view for the whole hotel
cards.note: Buying stock must be ONE action that both adds it to the shelf and records the money out — never typed twice, or the profit figure comes out wrong. Maintenance, tools and equipment are plain expenses. Then a single performance view adds everything up grouped by business area: Rooms, Restaurant, Bar, Gazebo, Garden, Parking. It is a view over the other parts, not a system holding its own numbers.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k91 · Block dates from the calendar toolbar — and show the reason on the calendar
cards.note:
Owner reports blocking a date is buried: you must pick dates, press New booking, and only then does the Block dates toggle appear inside the booking form.

Plan (agreed in discussion, NOT built yet):
- Add a Block dates button to the calendar toolbar beside New booking / Corporate / Log old booking, disabled until a unit + date range is picked — the same rule the other buttons already use.
- Reasons as one-tap chips: Cleaning · Maintenance · Owner use (family stays, e.g. Room 10). Free text kept for anything unusual.
- The reason becomes the calendar label: the pill should read "Cleaning" or "Owner use", not "Admin Date Block". Today the typed reason is stored in notes and shown nowhere (TimelineCell prints guest_name only).
- Remove the Booking/Block toggle from the booking form header so the action has one home, and move block into its own small modal like LogOldBookingModal.

Caveat to explain in the form: a block covers nights, not days (check-in must be before check-out), so a cleaning block for today also closes the room tonight.

Connected to k72 — a Cleaning block should create the housekeeping job itself.
cards.label: Feedback

cards.title: k93 · Bookings with no check-out date — the app forces one the paper log never needed
cards.note:
Raised by the owner from the old paper booking logs: at booking time staff often took a check-in and never wrote a check-out, and most paper bookings have no check-out date at all. The reason is not yet known — the owner is asking the staff first, before any change, and does not want to go against their workflow.

What the app does today: it FORCES a check-out before a booking can be saved (checkIn < checkOut is enforced in the booking form, again in isRoomAvailable, and a third time by the database exclusion constraint). So the app introduced a rule the paper process never had.

Why an end is needed — not stubbornness, and useful for the staff conversation:
- The calendar draws a booking by walking day by day from check-in to check-out (CalendarTab.tsx lines 62-70). No check-out = no end = the pill draws nothing, so the booking is invisible.
- The overlap check needs an end too: with an empty check-out the date comparisons fail silently and isRoomAvailable returns AVAILABLE, so the room would look free on every date and could be double-booked.

Questions to ask the staff (the answer changes the fix):
1. Did the guest not know how long they were staying — booked a night at a time?
2. Was that column the departure as it happened, written when they left and blank until then?
3. Was it simply not needed — the room was held until the key came back?

Ways to honour the habit without breaking the calendar:
- Ask "how many nights?" instead of an end date. Book 1 night by default, extend in one tap (ExtendStayModal already exists). Closest fit for a pension house.
- An "open stay" booking: no fixed departure, the room stays blocked from check-in onward until the stay is closed, and the calendar shows a "still here" bar to today. Needs real work on the overlap logic — no end means the room is blocked for everything after check-in.
- Both: default to nights, allow open stay when the guest truly does not know.

Do NOT build until the owner has talked to the staff.
cards.label: Feedback

cards.title: k105 · A screen to edit the restaurant menu and prices
cards.note:
The menu is in the database now (`menu_categories` + `menu_items`, seeded with the hotel's 61 items). What is missing is a screen: change a price, add a dish, retire one — without a developer and without a SQL run.

Natural home: Settings → a "Restaurant Menu" tab next to Shared Rates, or the Restaurant tab itself. Editing writes through `saveMenu` (`utils/restaurantMenu.ts`), which already upserts the whole list for every device.

Depends on nothing; the data layer is done.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k107 · Photos of the dishes on the menu tiles
cards.note:
Right now each dish tile shows a lucide icon for its food group (a coffee cup for Breakfast, a beer mug for Beer). A photo of the actual dish would be far more visual and faster to recognise — the owner asked for a more visual till.

Needs: somewhere to store the images (Supabase Storage), an upload path in the menu editor (see the edit-screen card), and a fallback to the icon when a dish has no photo.

Held back until there are real pictures — a grid of mismatched stock photos is worse than clean icons.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k109 · Cooking choices on a dish (buttered / sinagang / tinola)
cards.note:
Shrimp, Tuna, Pampano and the Mix Vegetable salad come with a choice the guest picks at the counter — buttered / sinagang / tinola / fried. Today the choices live in the tile's tooltip and the staff member just says them out loud, so the bill does not record which one was ordered, and the kitchen slip could not either.

Wanted: tapping such a dish asks for the choice, and the line reads `Shrimp · Sinagang` on the tab, the bill and the kitchen slip. Needs a small `choices` field on `menu_items` (the `note` column already holds the list today).

Worth doing before the restaurant opens, but not before the till works.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k120 · Receipt prints the receipt, not the booking behind it
cards.note:
BUG B1 (md line 5). Pressing Print on a payment receipt sent the booking slide-over to the printer instead of the 58 mm slip.

FIXED in code: papers now mark themselves in `src/index.css` (`.print-slip` for the 58 mm roll, `.print-page` for the guest bill) and everything else steps aside for the print. Classes added to PaymentReceiptDocument, SlipModal and InvoiceDocument.

Left open only for the owner to try it and close the card himself.
cards.label: bug

cards.title: k124 · "Prepared by" on the bill and the receipt
cards.note:
BUG B2 (md line 8). A name typed in "Receptionist on duty" never reaches the printed statement or receipt.

The app sends it, the mappers carry `prepared_by`, and both printed documents read it — so the name is lost on the way to the database (the booking RPCs are the drifted ones).

Waiting on one row from the owner's Supabase: the diagnostic query in `.lavish/new-notes.html` (bookings_in_db / with_prepared_by / tabs_in_db / rooms_with_promo / bookings_on_promo). If `with_prepared_by` is 0, rebuild `book_booking`/`update_booking` from the live definition with `prepared_by` added.
cards.label: bug

comments.content:
**Solved — and it was bigger than the name.**

The owner's two database answers settled it: `book_booking` and `update_booking` both handle `prepared_by` (so it is not lost on the way in), and 6 bookings have a name stored. That means the name was being **wiped after it was saved**.

Root cause: `useRealtimeBookings.ts` → `rowToBooking`, the mapper that rebuilds a booking from the live database row. Its column list had fallen behind the app's own list (`toBookingRecord` in `utils/db.ts`), and `prepared_by` was not in it. So every live INSERT/UPDATE replaced the cached booking with one that had no `prepared_by` — and because the cache is what the quick view saves back, the next save (recording a payment, checking a guest in, extending a stay) wrote the booking back **without the name**, erasing it in the database too. That is why only 6 of 32 bookings still had one.

The same gap was silently wiping, on every live event and the save that followed:
`actual_check_in` / `actual_check_out` (the in-house state — which also decides whether a guest's food tab is unlocked), `payment_records` (the numbered receipts), `applied_discount`, `notes` (the block reason), `early_check_in_hours` / `late_check_out_hours`, `venue_day_blocks`, `breakfast_days`, and `birthdate`.

All eleven columns are now mapped. `npx tsc -b --force` exits 0. No SQL needed — the fix is app-side. The rule is in `src/AGENTS.md`: a booking column must be added in three places (the `Booking` type, `toBookingRecord`, `rowToBooking`).

cards.title: k144 · Guest bill on A5
cards.note: md line 9. The Guest Billing Statement is laid out for A5 paper instead of A4. The payment receipt keeps its 58 mm thermal roll. Note: the same statement is also emailed (see the email card), so the email copy should match the A5 layout.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k146 · Email the bill and the receipt, from your Gmail
cards.note: Owner: "send only when staff presses a button. We have gmail." Nothing is emailed automatically: staff press **Email to guest** on the statement and on a receipt, and the guest gets it from the hotel's Gmail account. Needs a Gmail app password (or an SMTP-capable sender), and a Supabase edge function to send with the PDF attached. Owner to supply the account details when this is built.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k148 · Vacation House: ₱2,000 reservation + ₱2,000 safety deposit
cards.note:
md line 23. Owner approved: a flat **₱2,000 reservation** for the Vacation House, never "half", taken off the house rate — plus a **₱2,000 safety deposit**.

Agreed handling: both collected with the reservation and printed as two separate lines (₱2,000 + ₱2,000 = ₱4,000 up front); the safety deposit is handed back at check-out as a refund line on the bill — "Safety deposit returned ₱2,000" — only once staff confirm no damage. If there is damage, the amount kept is typed and a line says why. The check-out refund flow is new.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k150 · A photo of the payment, with the reference read from it
cards.note:
Owner: "guests can send the screenshot of the payment that has the reference no. or just take a picture if they are physically right beside them... the photo should be kept, while the reference no. field gets filled because of the AI extracting it."

So: the payment confirmation PHOTO is stored as proof, and the reference number box is filled by AI reading the photo — staff can correct what it read. Works both ways: a guest sends a screenshot ahead (portal), or the desk photographs a phone at the counter. Needs image storage (Supabase storage bucket) plus an AI reading step (a paid API, with typing still possible when it cannot read).
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k152 · Tables as pills — several per tab, edited in Settings
cards.note:
md line 27. Owner: "sometimes they use more than 1 table so an order would use 2 tables or more. and yes, it should be editable in the settings."

Opening a walk-in tab offers the tables as tappable pills instead of a typed box — one table or several for the same tab. A table already on a running tab shows as taken and cannot be picked twice; it frees up when that tab is settled. The list of tables lives in Settings, where tables can be added or retired.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k156 · Airbnb / Booking.com / Agoda — parked last
cards.note: md line 6. Owner: "suspend airbnb, booking, agoda development. last on the list of things to work on." Nothing is deleted — the iCal sync work simply sits at the very bottom of the queue until the owner says otherwise. The k69 restaurant work came first, as he also said.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k128 · One price — stop calling it a promo
cards.note:
Owner: "Just remove the regular price. there's only 1 price now which is the promo. but let's not call it that. it's the new regular now." And on the promo ON/OFF switch: "remove it".

The promo figure becomes THE price everywhere: no crossed-out regular, no promo badge, no "Use Promo Price" switch, no header toggle. Settings keeps one price per room and one per venue, and the printed bills follow. Retiring the toggle also means `promoMode`/`promo_applied` and the promo columns stop being part of pricing.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k138 · Add-ons behind a More button, suited to the room or venue
cards.note: Owner: "I like a more button. I just meant everything should be accessible but not immediately on display." Everything stays reachable behind a **More add-ons** button, and the list is trimmed to suit the unit: a room shows linens, toiletries, an extra bed and breakfast; a venue (Gazebo, Garden, Vacation House) shows tables, chairs, tent, mineral water and extra hours. No guest is ever offered a tent for a room. Approved by the owner.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k136 · The receptionist's name remembers itself
cards.note: Owner: "I like the receptionist's name." The "Receptionist on duty" box suggests names already used (from past bookings), so the same person is never spelled two ways. Nationality and the other boxes stay plain for now — the owner is not sure about them yet.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k142 · Breakfast folded into the room line on the bill
cards.note: md line 14. On the guest bill and the payment receipt, a room with breakfast prints as ONE line — "Room 2 · Breakfast" — with the breakfast amount already inside the room rate. Breakfast stops having its own row anywhere. Follows from the card above (breakfast charged once, inside the rate). Touches utils/statement.ts, InvoiceDocument and PaymentReceiptDocument.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k134 · Open the new booking in the quick view after the bill
cards.note: md lines 10 and 20. After a booking is created the printable Guest Billing Statement comes first, as it does now; once that statement is printed or closed, the booking just created opens in the quick view instead of leaving staff on the calendar to hunt for it. With 2+ units, the first booking of the group opens.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k140 · Breakfast: ₱150 × the room's beds, once, inside the room rate
cards.note:
BUILT — and the rule changed after this card was written. Read this before checking it.

Original ask: "Forget about heads. just 150 times the amount of beds" + "breakfast is only charged once, which is added in the rate of the room".

What actually shipped (the owner's later decision): breakfast is one charge for the WHOLE stay at each ROOM'S OWN breakfast price, typed per room in Settings → Room Rates (blank until the desk types it). There is NO bed count and no x150 anywhere — a room with no price sells no breakfast, and its chip in the booking form cannot be ticked. The bed-count idea and its migration (add_room_beds) are dropped.

Where it lives: RoomRatesEditor (a Breakfast box per room) → set_room_breakfast_price; pricing.ts charges it once for the rooms the desk ticked (breakfast_included on that room's booking row); BreakfastRoomChips picks the rooms (tick = on, empty circle = off, "no price" rooms are not tappable, and a line under the row says what it adds up to); the guest portal offers the same switch for the room being booked; the per-day BreakfastRecorder is retired and no longer rendered; legacy breakfast_records still price old bookings.

Verified in code on 20 Sep. If the behaviour matches when you try it, this card can be closed — the ₱150 × beds wording above is history, not the rule.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
Built. Breakfast is now one charge for the stay: **₱150 × the room's beds**, folded into the room rate — never per person, never per day.

- `pricing.ts` charges it that way whenever the room has a bed count; a room with no count yet keeps the older per-person figures, so nothing changes for it until the desk writes the number down.
- `statement.ts` puts it **on the room line** — the row reads "Room 2 · Breakfast" and its amount includes the breakfast, with no separate breakfast row (k142).
- The day-by-day `BreakfastRecorder` is **retired** and no longer shown in the booking quick view (the file stays until the desk confirms the change).
- Settings → Room Rates now has a **Beds** box per room, next to the single price, and the editor writes both stored price columns with the same figure.

**Run `supabase/migrations/20260918120000_add_room_beds.sql`** — it adds `rooms.beds` and the writer `set_room_beds`. Until it runs, savings of the bed count stay in the browser and breakfast keeps the old rule.

`npx tsc -b --force` exits 0.

Follow-up built after the owner's question — breakfast is now the ROOM's choice, not the guest's.

**In the booking form.** One line of room chips (`BreakfastRoomChips`, new) above Add-ons: `[Room 3 · ₱300] [Room 5] [All]`. It builds **OFF** (the owner's choice), a tapped room turns gold and shows what it adds — ₱150 × that room's beds — and the amount is never worked out by hand. It writes `breakfast_included` on each room's own booking row (no new column).

**Removed.** The booker's breakfast tick-box, the companion B'fast tick, and the **Breakfast column on the printed companion table**.

**Guest portal.** The public `/reserve` page now offers the same switch for the room being booked, priced live and saved on that booking.

**Old bookings untouched.** `pricing.ts` gives `breakfast_records` priority, so a booking made while breakfast was recorded day by day keeps the figure it was actually charged; only new bookings follow the room's flag.

`npx tsc -b --force` exits 0. The bed count still needs `supabase/migrations/20260918120000_add_room_beds.sql` — a room with no bed count keeps its old breakfast until it is filled in.

cards.title: k122 · The booking charges the price it shows (promo)
cards.note:
BUG B3 (md line 13) — the first fix note here is obsolete; the real root cause was found on 20 Sep while testing a booking called SEB.

Original symptom: the calendar showed promo prices while the booking form charged the regular ones. Fixed at the time by initialising the form from the promo switch.

What was really wrong (found 20 Sep): when the promo switch was retired (card k128) nothing recorded which price a booking was made at. `createManualBooking` wrote `promo_applied: usePromo ?? undefined`, and the form passes no usePromo, so every new booking saved `undefined` — while every read path (quick view / recomputeBalance, printed statement, analytics, calendar extend) reads `promo_applied === true`. So a booking was CREATED at the single price and RE-READ at the old regular one. A guest who had paid in full came back as "Partly paid · ₱2,850 of ₱3,800 · ₱950 still to receive", and the printed bill would have said ₱3,800 too.

Fixed: `createManualBooking` now records `promo_applied: usePromo ?? true` (a booking made without a price choice IS the single price); the guest portal records `promo_applied: true`; the retired sale mode (`isPromoActive`/`setPromoActive`/`daweez_promo_active`) is deleted; the crossed-out old price is gone from the calendar labels and the portal cards; and the audit that followed removed the last "promo" wording from the printed bill (" · promo" room label), the bill's "Discount/Promos" header, the portal's "Promo Price" line and Settings' "Regular and Promo" sentence.

Rows saved BEFORE the fix still carry no marker: re-saving one (Edit booking → Confirm) records it and re-prices it at the single figure, so it reads Paid. Verified in code; needs the owner's retest — make a booking, record the deposit, record the rest, and it must go green.
cards.label: bug

comments.content:
Regression of this exact bug, found by the owner while testing (booking "SEB"): a booking was MADE at the single price but every later screen re-priced it at the old regular price, so a guest who had paid in full came back as "Partly paid" and the printed bill disagreed with the booking form.

Cause: the walk-in form and the guest portal stopped storing a price marker when the promo switch was retired (card k128). `createManualBooking` wrote `promo_applied: usePromo ?? undefined`, and the form passes no `usePromo`, so every new booking saved `undefined`; every read path (`recomputeBalance`, `statement.ts`, `useAnalyticsCalculations`, `CalendarTab` extend) computes `promo_applied === true`, so it fell through to `base_price` (the retired regular figure) while creation had used `promo_price` (the single figure).

Fixed:
- `createManualBooking` now records `promo_applied: usePromo ?? true` — a booking made without a price choice IS the single price; Log old booking still passes its explicit Regular/Promo choice (and now passes it through, so a paper log keeps the figure it was logged at).
- The guest portal stores `promo_applied: true` too (it was also leaving it undefined).
- The retired sale mode is fully gone: `isPromoActive`/`setPromoActive`/`daweez_promo_active` deleted, and the crossed-out regular price removed from the calendar room labels and the portal cards (both were also showing `base_price` when the switch was off — a second, wrong price on screen).
Rows saved before this fix keep `promo_applied` undefined; re-saving one (Edit booking → Confirm) records the marker and re-prices it at the single figure. npx tsc -b --force exits 0.

cards.title: k130 · Deposit: half by default, typable
cards.note:
Owner: "the custom deposit amount is an option, but default is always half." Every booking takes a deposit to hold the room.

The deposit box arrives filled with half the stay and can be overwritten with any peso amount. The typed amount then flows through the printed statement ("Amount Due"), `amountToPayNow`, and the arrival step — so the desk asks for exactly what was agreed.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
Built. The deposit is now a figure the desk can set, not just "half".

- `agreed_deposit` (new column on `bookings`) keeps the amount agreed at booking; `amountToPayNow` asks for exactly that figure, capped at what is actually owed, instead of recomputing half.
- **Run `supabase/migrations/20260917120000_add_agreed_deposit.sql`** — it adds the column and one small SECURITY DEFINER writer (`set_booking_agreed_deposit`). That writer exists because `book_booking`/`update_booking` are the drifted jsonb functions and would otherwise need rebuilding from the live definition; a failure to save the deposit is non-fatal and simply leaves the default.
- `BookingDepositFields` (new, in `walk-in/`) replaces the old billing step: the box arrives filled with half the stay, can be typed over, and shows the whole stay in words so nobody has to do the maths. It also keeps the edit-mode corrections (already received, balance due, security deposit, invoice number).
- `src/types/booking.ts`, `toBookingRecord`, `rowToBooking` and `createManualBooking` all carry the new field — the three-places rule the docs now spell out.

`npx tsc -b --force` exits 0.

Follow-up from the owner's test (21 Sep): with Room 4 at ₱950 and breakfast ₱300 on a TWO-night stay, the deposit box said "Half the stay is ₱1,100 — the whole stay comes to ₱2,200", and it read as if breakfast had been added wrongly (950 + 300 ≠ 2,200).

The arithmetic was right — 2 nights × ₱950 = ₱1,900 + ₱300 breakfast = ₱2,200, half = ₱1,100 — but the box never showed its working, so the nights had to be reverse-engineered. It now prints the sum:

  2 nights · Room ₱1,900 · Breakfast ₱300
  Whole stay ₱2,200 — half of it is ₱1,100.

If the nights are ever wrong, that line shows it instead of hiding it.

cards.title: k132 · The guest chooses how they pay, not the staff
cards.note:
Owner: "the staff don't get to decide what type of payment method the guest will use, only the guest get to choose that."

The booking form stops demanding a payment method (it is currently REQUIRED and blocks the save). The method is the guest's choice, recorded when the money is actually received — which is already how each payment record works. Printed statements therefore name the method only once it is known.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
NEW REQUIREMENT from the owner's review (20 Sep, on the audit page) — k132 is NOT ready to close until this is in and tested.

His words, in short: the printed Guest Billing Statement is where the guest chooses Cash / GCash / Bank transfer (it already prints the boxes when no method is known). The guest then tells the desk — "I sent it by GCash", or they see the cash handed over. Because the choice is the guest's, the STAFF must be able to enter or update that method on the booking, and it must come out on the payment receipt.

What shipped for it: the quick view now carries a "Guest pays by" row (src/components/calendar/GuestMethodPicker.tsx) with Cash / GCash / Bank transfer / Other as tick-chips, wired to the booking's own `payment_method` and saved the moment the desk taps it — no money has to be recorded for it. The caption says whose choice it is ("Guest chose GCash"), and that it prints on the bill and on the receipt for the money recorded. Each recorded payment still carries its own method (the guest may settle the rest a different way), and the receipt prints that payment's method.

Also cleaned out of ExtendStayModal while here: the dead `stayDays` / `breakfastRecords` / dateToString leftovers from the retired per-day BreakfastRecorder.

Typecheck passes; the only lint error left in that file is the pre-existing setState-in-effect one. To test: open a booking → tap a method → print the bill (it must name it) → record a payment (the receipt must name it) → change the method and print again.

Three follow-ups from the owner's test of the Guest pays by row — all built:

1. **"Other" removed.** The chips are Cash / GCash / Bank transfer only (and the same three now appear in the payment form, the arrival step and the "record a payment" form). An "Other" bucket hid how the guest actually paid.
2. **GCash and Bank transfer now require a reference number.** Tapping either reveals a "reference no." box with the inline red note; the method is saved with the reference (the reference is stored on the booking's `payment_reference`, so the bill and the receipt can print it). Cash saves on the tap, because it needs no proof.
3. **BUG FIXED — the receipt said "Cash" on a GCash booking.** The money card seeded its method once when the panel opened (`agreedMethod(booking)`), and `paymentMethodLabel('')` falls back to 'Cash' — so tapping GCash in the picker updated the booking but not the method the first payment used. `savePaymentMethod` now also updates the payment's method and reference whenever nothing has been recorded yet, and the reference the guest already gave (e.g. from the online portal) starts filled in.

Test again: tap GCash → enter the ref → Save method → the bill must name GCash + ref → record the money → the receipt must say GCash with that reference.

Round three — the owner reworked the whole quick view (21 Sep). Built exactly as asked:

1. **"Balance on arrival" removed from the printed bill.** He did not know what it meant on a ₱1,250 booking with a ₱625 deposit, and it read as a second demand. The Amount Due figure now names itself ("Deposit (50%)" / "Remaining balance") and nothing else is added under it.
2. **"Save method" button deleted.** The flow is now: tap GCash → type the reference → press the confirm button below → receipt prints. Tapping a method writes it down; the reference saves when the box is left; no separate save step to wonder about.
3. **No circles / ticks / emoji on the method buttons.** Cash · GCash · Bank transfer, plain words; the chosen one is gold and bold, nothing else.
4. **The quick view is choices, not orders.** The money card only reports (chip, whole stay total, amount to pay, progress bar) — it no longer has its own method picker or reference box, and it never shouts "Receive money & check in". Under it sit three separate choices: `Receive ₱X & print receipt`, `Check in` (disabled with its reason while money is owed) and `Check out`. `ReceivePaymentStep` is retired — the extra guided step was the confusing part.
5. **After the money is received the quick view closes**, once the receipt is dismissed: the errand is done and the desk is back at the calendar, instead of holding a booking they have finished with.
6. **The Guest tab is hidden until the guest is checked in** — nobody orders before check-in, so it no longer appears locked.

Files: ExtendStayModal, BookingMoneyPanel (rewritten as a status card), GuestMethodPicker (rewritten), InvoiceDocument. Typecheck passes; lint clean on all of them. Not to be closed until he has run the GCash flow and the partly-paid flow once more.

Check-in reverting (found while testing, fixed).

Symptom: check a guest in → the button becomes Check out, but closing the quick view and opening the booking again showed Check in.

Cause: the timeline cell's React.memo comparator only compared id / status / payment_status, so a save that changed only actual_check_in (or actual_check_out) was treated as "props equal" and the cell kept the older booking object. That stale object is what the pill hands to the quick view on click — so the panel opened pre-check-in, while the money (which had changed payment_status) refreshed fine.

Two fixes:
1. CalendarTab now opens the slide-over on the live row (bookings.find by id), so a stale snapshot can never reach the panel again.
2. The cell comparator now also compares actual_check_in / actual_check_out / both dates / guest name / downpayment_paid / balance_due / receipt count.

tsc and eslint clean. Worth a retest: check in, close, reopen — it must say Check out.

cards.title: k154 · The calendar starts at today
cards.note: md line 22. Owner picked option (b): the grid begins at today and runs into the days ahead, so the earlier days of the month are not on screen at all and there is nothing to scroll back through. Replaces the current whole-month grid that opens at the start of the month. Touches CalendarTab and TimelineGrid.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
Built (in Review). What shipped:
- The grid now opens on TODAY (Sun 20 Sep 2026 opens at Sep 20, not Sep 1). Earlier days of the month are not drawn at all, so nothing is scrolled past to find today.
- The window is 31 day columns and runs into the days ahead, so it never shrinks into a few stretched wide columns late in a month. A day that is the 1st of a month prints its month name beside the number ("1 Oct") with a gold left edge, and the toolbar header reads "20 Sep – 20 Oct 2026" when the window crosses a month.
- Toolbar: "This month" is now "Today" (jumps back to the current month, whose grid opens at today), with a small "from today" badge beside the title while the window really starts today.
- Month navigation still works as before (prev/next, month picker): any month you navigate to opens on its 1st. Nothing before today is ever the first column of the current month.
- A stay that began before the first column carries a small "‹" before the guest's name (tooltip: Already staying — arrived <date>), so a cut-off block is not read as a fresh arrival.
- The horizontal scroll snaps back to the left edge whenever the window changes, so today is never off screen.
Files: src/components/calendar/timelineDays.ts (new, pure day-list builder), CalendarTab.tsx, calendar/TimelineGrid.tsx, calendar/TimelineCell.tsx, calendar/CalendarToolbar.tsx. npx tsc -b --force exits 0. Reviewed visually on .lavish/k154-calendar-today.html.

cards.title: k69 · Guest tab — charge anything to the room
cards.note: The connection every other system needs: a running tab for the guest's stay. Any part can add a line to it (a restaurant lunch, an extra towel, a lost item) and read the total, so check-out adds everything up at once. Today the app only tracks the room's balance due; this widens it to room + restaurant + extras, minus payments. Build this first — everything else plugs into it.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
Decision changed by the owner (was: append-only, a wrong line is answered with a "correction" line).

Now: staff simply **delete** a mistaken line, with the app's own confirm — exactly how a wrong payment is already handled, so there is one money rule instead of two. Corrections are gone from the app; the `kind`/`corrects_line_id`/`reason` columns stay in the table but nothing writes them.

Done: new migration `20260913120000_allow_tab_line_delete.sql` (grants DELETE on tab_lines, makes the correction self-reference ON DELETE CASCADE), `deleteTabLine` in utils/tabs.ts, and the bin button replacing Fix in GuestTabPanel.

⚠️ The new SQL must be run in Supabase — until then the delete is refused by RLS.

Part C built — settling a walk-in tab at the counter.

Done: `settleTab` (utils/tabs.ts) records one numbered receipt on the tab (`payment_records`) and closes it; `TabSettlePanel` (amount = the tab's own total, method chips, reference only when the method needs one); `TabReceiptModal` prints the 58 mm slip; `RestaurantTab` shows the settle panel once something is on the tab and prints the receipt straight away. Shared slip pieces moved to `billing/receiptPrimitives.tsx` so the tab slip and the payment receipt cannot drift apart.

⚠️ Run `supabase/migrations/20260915120000_add_tab_payments.sql` in Supabase — until then the settle falls back to the browser store and the tab comes back open after a reload.

Still open on this card: (D) a mid-stay running tab printout, (E) restaurant money in the Earnings Report.

Parts D and E built — the card is finished on my side.

**D — the running tab on request.** `RunningTabSlip` + a quiet **Print the tab** button beside the running total in `GuestTabPanel` (shown whenever the panel is given its new `slip` prop). It prints a 58 mm slip headed *Running Tab* and stamped **NOT A RECEIPT**, ending with what happens next — *Settles with the room bill at check-out* on a stay, *Please settle this at the counter* on a walk-in. The shared print frame moved to `billing/SlipModal.tsx`, which `TabReceiptModal` now uses too, so all three slips look alike.

**E — restaurant money in the Earnings Report.** `getAllTabLines` (utils/tabs.ts) + `foodMoneyIn` (utils/tabRevenue.ts, day taken as a LOCAL date) feed `useAnalyticsCalculations`, which returns `restaurantTotal`. The report has a **Restaurant & bar** row and column, and that money is in Total Money In, Your Profit, the summary cards, the donut and Income Over Time. Counted on the day each order was placed, like a night is counted on the night it was slept.

`npx tsc -b --force` exits 0. Nothing on this card needs a new migration. Moving to Review for you to try.

Owner's review of the first build changed two things — both done.

**Orders now happen in the Restaurant screen, for both kinds of guest.** The owner's words: he wanted the restaurant to charge the room *in the restaurant*, not through a menu board squeezed into the tiny booking slide-over. So:
- `restaurant/GuestPicker.tsx` (new) — the list of guests who may be charged, i.e. checked in and not yet checked out (`inHouseGuests`), searchable by name or room, exporting `guestPlace`.
- `RestaurantTab` leads with that list; picking a guest opens their tab marked **On the room**, with **no counter settle panel** (their food joins the bill they already have).
- `GuestTabPanel` gained `ordering` + `onOpenTill`. The booking slide-over passes `ordering={false}`: lines, total, bin, print button, and *"Orders are taken in the Restaurant screen"* with a gold **Take orders for this guest** button.
- `utils/restaurantFocus.ts` (new) — the `focusGuestTab` / `takeFocusedGuestTab` hand-off so that button lands on the restaurant with the guest already open (read in an effect, not a state initializer: StrictMode runs those twice and would swallow it).

**Corrected understanding of the money.** A checked-in guest has already settled the rest of the stay, so the tab simply adds to a paid bill and is received at check-out — the deposit being room-only is a backstop, not a live scenario. My earlier worked example implied food could be inside the deposit base, which the check-in rule prevents.

`npx tsc -b --force` exits 0; no new SQL.

Owner queued "fix the three bugs first" from the new-notes review page. Two fixed, one blocked on one query.

**B1 — the receipt printed the booking instead of the receipt: fixed.** Printing used to send the whole screen behind the slip to the printer. Added a print rule in `src/index.css`: anything meant for paper marks itself (`.print-slip` for a 58 mm slip, `.print-page` for the guest bill), and everything else steps aside for the duration of the print. Classes added to `PaymentReceiptDocument`, `SlipModal` (the tab receipt and running tab) and `InvoiceDocument`.

**B3 — the promo did not change the room price: fixed.** `WalkInBookingForm`'s "Use Promo Price" switch started `false` no matter what the global promo switch said, so the calendar showed promo prices while the booking charged the regular ones. It now initialises from `isPromoActive()` (`utils/promoMode.ts`) and follows the promo state in `CorporateBookingForm` too; editing a booking sets it from `promo_applied`, so an old booking keeps the price it was made at rather than silently re-pricing.

**B2 — the "Prepared by" name is missing on the bill and the receipt: needs one query.** The form sends `preparedBy`, the RPC mapper and the local mapper both carry `prepared_by`, and both printed documents read it — so the name is lost on the way to the database (the booking RPCs are the drifted ones). The one-row diagnostic is on the new-notes review page.

`npx tsc -b --force` exits 0. No SQL needed for B1/B3.

cards.title: k126 · One booking form — no steps, no price summary
cards.note:
Owner: "Step 2 and 3 should move to step 1 now. so there are no more steps, and it's just 1 form with everything." Plus "remove the price summary in the 3rd step".

One long page like the paper form: guest, companions, unit and dates, add-ons (behind a More button), discount, receptionist, deposit and payment. The Total/Deposit/Balance summary block comes out — the printed statement carries those figures. Booking / Block dates switch stays at the top.

Touches WalkInBookingForm (already over the 300-line limit and flagged).
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: k70 · Restaurant / Bar system — orders and charge to room
cards.note: Menu, tables and orders — a basic POS. Two ways to close an order: charge it to the guest's room (it lands on their tab and is paid at check-out) or pay now at the counter. The bar uses the same screen. Depends on the guest tab, so it comes second.
cards.label: New Feature

comments.content:
First slice built — the menu half (the "orders" half is still to come).

Typed off the restaurant's printed menu (both sides of the photos), 58 items in 15 groups: Breakfast (6–10am), Value Meals, Rice, Appetizers, Chicken, Pork, Beef, Seafood, Noodles, Vegetables & Salad, Snacks, Desserts & Shakes, Drinks, Beer & Spirits.

`utils/restaurantMenu.ts` holds the list (`getMenu`/`saveMenu`, prices editable, seeded from `DEFAULT_MENU`), and `components/restaurant/MenuPicker.tsx` is the till: category buttons across the top, dishes as tiles, one tap = one line on the tab with the price filled in. It sits at the top of `GuestTabPanel`, so both a stay's tab and a walk-in's use the same board; the written row stays underneath for anything not on the menu.

⚠️ The menu lives in the browser today (localStorage), like the breakfast menu — so two tablets would show two menus and clearing the browser loses a price change. Needs its own Supabase table before it is trusted as a till.

Still to come for this card: modifiers (the cooking choices on Shrimp/Tuna/Pampano), the table/order layer, and printing a kitchen slip.

Redesigned to the shape you picked from the drawn options (P2), and the till now looks like the menu card.

What changed on /restaurant:
- One strip across the top — "Being served" — everyone you may charge in one row: the diner tabs at the counter first, then every guest who is in the hotel. Each shows their name, their place and what they owe so far ("—" when nothing is ordered yet). A Find box filters the row; "+ New diner" opens the name/table form only when a diner is being seated.
- The bill sits on the left of whoever you tapped: the lines with a bin on each, the total, and Print the tab (58 mm). A room guest is marked On the room and is received at check-out; a diner pays at the counter and gets the settle panel once something is on the tab.
- The menu is now THE MENU CARD: off-white paper, house name across the top, each category centred between its own rules, dish on the left with dotted leaders to the price on the right, cooking choices printed in italic under the dish, two columns, one scroll. No category buttons anywhere. The whole line is the tap target and a dish already on the bill keeps its count on that line.

Under the hood: `TabBill` (the bill), `useTabOrder` (the only place a line is written) and `OffMenuOrder` are shared with the booking quick view, so the two screens cannot drift; `getOpenTabs` reads every open tab in one query; the old `GuestPicker` list was retired (its helpers moved to `served.ts`). Nothing about the money rules changed — the tab still joins the bill at check-out and the deposit stays stay-only.

Verified: `npx tsc -b --force` and `npx eslint` both clean.

Still open on this card's follow-ups: k105 (edit the menu and prices), k109 (real cooking-choice buttons), k152 (tables as pills).

Follow-up from testing the built screen (tablet in front of the guest): the dish rows were too thin to tap with a finger.

Done now:
- Every dish on the menu card is a **48px row** whatever its text — the whole row is the target, not the name.
- Dish name 13.5px, price 14px, cooking choice 10.5px; the count badge is bigger too.
- The category headings got more room above them, so the card breathes while scrolling.
- The same treatment on the rest of the till, since it is all finger work: the "Being served" chips and "+ New diner" are 44px, the bill's bin is a proper tap target, "Print the tab" and "Add" on the written row are 44px, and the new-diner form's buttons match.

Also fixed while in there: the two menu columns are now cut in half by item count instead of dealt to whichever side was shortest, so the menu reads straight down the left column and then the right, the way a printed card reads (before, the categories zig-zagged across the fold).

`tsc` and `eslint` clean.

Added at your request: a **Find a dish** box above the menu card (44px, with an ✕ to clear).

- It filters by dish name **and** the cooking note, so "buttered" or "silang" finds the right Shrimp/Tuna line.
- What is left keeps its category heading, its dotted leader, its price and its count badge — it is still the same card, just narrowed.
- The card's subtitle says how many matched ("4 dishes match “sili”").
- Nothing found says so and points at **+ Something not on the menu** underneath.

It lives above the card on purpose, so the card itself stays a paper menu.

`tsc` and `eslint` clean.
